children: Motilal Oswal's research report on Indian Bank

Indian Bank (INBK) reported a 2QFY27 PAT of INR34.6b, up 15% YoY/6% QoQ (in line), as a one-off gain in other income was utilized to create a provisioning buffer (additional ECL provision of INR15b created against the INR13.8b gain from the sale and revaluation of its NSE stake). NII grew 18% YoY/4% QoQ to INR77.2b (in line with our est. of INR76.4b). NIM improved by 2bp QoQ to 3.31% (in line). Advances grew 17.5% YoY/5.7% QoQ, while deposits rose 12.5% YoY/3.5% QoQ. Consequently, the C/D ratio rose by 171bp to 81.4%. Domestic CASA came in slightly lower at 39.4% vs. 39.7% in 1QFY27. Slippages declined to INR12b from INR13b in 1QFY27. The bank made additional floating provisions of INR15b for the ECL transition (cumulative INR25b), with further residual provisions of INR10b expected. GNPA/NNPA ratios improved by 25bp/1bp QoQ to 1.61%/0.14%. PCR stood at 91.5%.
We raise our earnings estimates by ~3% for FY27/FY28 and estimate the bank to deliver an FY28E RoA/RoE of 1.4%/18.7%. Reiterate BUY with an unchanged TP of INR1,025 (premised on 1.4x Mar’28E ABV).
